claims.text: The proposed material is a tungsten-containing NbMoTaW high-entropy alloy.
Nb, Mo, Ta, and W are present in nominally equal atomic percentages.
The synthesized NbMoTaW alloy is a refractory solid solution.
The as-synthesized NbMoTaW alloy is homogenized and has a uniform elemental distribution.
The as-synthesized NbMoTaW alloy has a stable refractory phase.
Electrochemical activation or mild surface conditioning will expose active tungsten and other elemental sites.
The proposed surface activation can expose active sites without compromising alloy integrity.
The catalyst will be tested in acidic electrolyte, exemplified by 0.5 M H2SO4, at ambient or moderately elevated temperature.
Combining W with Nb, Mo, and Ta generates a locally altered electronic environment at the alloy surface.
Multi-element alloying modifies the electronic states of the catalyst surface.
The modified surface electronic states lower the energy barrier for hydrogen adsorption and desorption.
Refractory components of NbMoTaW possess corrosion resistance under prolonged electrochemical cycling.
Corrosion resistance of the refractory components improves catalyst durability.
NbMoTaW will have enhanced HER and HOR catalytic activity relative to conventional catalysts.
NbMoTaW will achieve lower HER and HOR overpotentials than standard Pt-based catalysts.
NbMoTaW will retain catalytic activity over extended cycling better than standard Pt-based catalysts.
The direct translation of refractory-alloy durability into enhanced HER and HOR activity has not yet been established.
Optimization of the surface treatment may be required because interactions between microstructure and the electrochemical environment are uncertain.
The inherent durability of tungsten and refractory HEA compositions under extreme conditions suggests possible electrochemical durability benefits.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires lower overpotentials than Pt, whereas the falsification rule treats overpotentials merely comparable to Pt as sufficient to avoid falsification. Comparable performance does not establish the claimed enhancement.
